name: ABS
keywords: returns the absolute value of the specified number. abs(num) -> decimal

name: ADD_DAYS
keywords: returns a date or datetime adjusted by the specified number of days, either forward (positive) or backward (negative), relative to the provided date or datetime. add_days(date/datetime, num) -> date/datetime

name: ADD_MONTHS
keywords: returns a date or datetime adjusted by the specified number of months, either forward (positive) or backward (negative), relative to the provided date or datetime. add_months(date/datetime, num) -> date/datetime

name: AND
keywords: returns true if all provided conditions are true; otherwise, returns false. and(...logical) -> boolean

name: BASE64_ENCODE
keywords: returns the base64-encoded representation of the provided string. base64_encode(string) -> string

name: BASE64_DECODE
keywords: returns the original string by decoding the provided base64-encoded input. if the input is not valid base64, the function returns an error. base64_decode(encoding) -> string

name: BLANK_VALUE
keywords: if the value is blank, evaluates the substitute values in order and returns the first non-blank value; otherwise, returns the original value. a value is considered blank if it is null, empty, contains only whitespace, or evaluates to $skip_assignment. blank_value(value, ...substitute_value) -> object

name: BUSINESS_HOURS_ADD
keywords: adds a time interval to a starting datetime, counting only business hours. the result is returned in gmt. business_hours_add(start_date, interval_milliseconds, business_hours_name_optional) -> datetime

name: BUSINESS_HOURS_DIFF
keywords: calculates the difference in milliseconds between two datetime values within business hours. uses the default schedule if none is provided. business_hours_diff(start_date, end_date, business_hours_name_optional) -> long

name: BUSINESS_HOURS_IS_WITHIN
keywords: returns true if the specified datetime is within defined business hours. business_hours_is_within(target_date, business_hours_name_optional) -> boolean

name: BUSINESS_HOURS_NEXT_START_DATE
keywords: returns the next datetime business hours open after the specified target date; returns the target date itself if it's within business hours. the result is returned in gmt. business_hours_next_start_date(target_date, business_hours_name_optional) -> datetime

name: CASE
keywords: returns the corresponding return_value for the first compare_value equal to the provided value. if no values match, returns default_return_value_optional. if default_return_value_optional is omitted and no matches occur, the function returns $skip_assignment. case(value, ...[compare_value, return_value], default_return_value_optional) -> object

name: CEILING
keywords: returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the specified number. ceiling(num) -> decimal

name: CHAR
keywords: returns the character corresponding to the specified ascii code. char(int) -> string

name: CONTAINS
keywords: returns true if the provided string contains any of the specified compare_strings. the comparison is case-sensitive. otherwise, returns false. contains(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: CONTAINS_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns true if the provided string contains any of the specified compare_strings, ignoring case differences. otherwise, returns false. contains_ignore_case(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: COS
keywords: returns the trigonometric cosine of the specified angle. cos(num) -> decimal

name: DATE
keywords: returns a date constructed from the specified year, month, and day components. date(year, month, day) -> date

name: DAY
keywords: returns the day of the month from a date or datetime in the context user's local time zone. day(date/datetime) -> integer

name: DAYS_BETWEEN
keywords: returns the number of days between two provided dates. the result is positive if end_date occurs after start_date, negative if it occurs before, and zero if the dates are identical. days_between(start_date, end_date) -> integer

name: DAY_OF_YEAR
keywords: returns the day number within the year for a given date, ranging from 1 to 365 or 366. day_of_year(date) -> integer

name: DISTANCE
keywords: calculates the distance between two locations in kilometers. distance(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) -> double

name: ENDS_WITH
keywords: returns true if the provided string ends with any of the specified compare_strings. the comparison is case-sensitive. otherwise, returns false. ends_with(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: ENDS_WITH_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns true if the provided string ends with any of the specified compare_strings. the comparison is case-insensitive. otherwise, returns false. ends_with_ignore_case(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: EQUALS
keywords: returns true if the value matches any of the given compare_values (case-sensitive); otherwise, returns false. equals(value, ...compare_values) -> boolean

name: EQUALS_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns true if the value matches any of the given compare_values (case-insensitive); otherwise, returns false. equals_ignore_case(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: ERROR
keywords: throws an exception with a custom message, optionally based on a specified condition. if a condition is provided, an exception is thrown only if the condition evaluates to true. error(…[message, condition_optional]) -> error

name: ERROR_VALUE
keywords: returns the substitute value if evaluating the value results in an error; otherwise, returns the original value. error_value(value, substitute_value) -> object

name: ESCAPE_HTML4
keywords: returns a string with characters escaped according to html 4 standards. converts special html characters into their corresponding html entities to safely display as literal text in web pages. escape_html4(string) -> string

name: ESCAPE_XML
keywords: returns a string with special xml characters replaced by their corresponding xml entities. useful for safely including strings within xml documents. escape_xml(string) -> string

name: EVALUATE
keywords: returns the value of a formula stored in a custom field, evaluated at runtime. optionally retrieves fields from related records. evaluate(formula_string, retrieve_source_fields, relationship_name_optional) -> object

name: EXP
keywords: returns the value of e raised to the specified number. exp(num) -> decimal

name: EVALUATED_FIELD_VALUE
keywords: returns the evaluated value of a mapped target field that has already been processed prior to the current field’s evaluation within the executable’s mapping step. if the field has not yet been evaluated, the function returns null. evaluated_field_value(mapped_target_field_name) -> object

name: FLOOR
keywords: returns the largest integer less than or equal to the specified number. floor(num) -> decimal

name: FORMAT_DATETIME
keywords: formats a date or datetime as a string. format_datetime(date/datetime, format_string_optional, timezone_optional) -> string

name: FORMAT_JSON_TEMPLATE
keywords: parses and formats a json template string by resolving embedded expressions and merge fields into json-formatted output. format_json_template(template) -> string

name: FORMAT_STRING_TEMPLATE
keywords: parses and formats a template string by resolving embedded expressions and merge fields into standard string output. format_string_template(template) -> string

name: GET_PICKLIST_FIELD_OPTIONS
keywords: returns a list of options for the specified picklist field on a given object. get_picklist_field_options(object_name, field_name) -> string[]

name: HAS_DUPLICATES
keywords: returns true if the current source record has duplicate records identified by matching rules configured in salesforce duplicate management. has_duplicates() -> boolean

name: HAS_PERMISSION
keywords: returns true if the context user has any of the specified custom permissions. otherwise, returns false. has_permission(...custom_permission_names)-> boolean

name: HOUR
keywords: extracts the hour (0–23) from a datetime value, based on the context user’s local time zone. hour(datetime) -> integer

name: HOUR_GMT
keywords: extracts the hour (0–23) from a datetime value, based on gmt. hour_gmt(datetime) -> integer

name: HTML_TABLE
keywords: generates a formatted html table string from records of the specified source object, filtered by matching field-value pairs and an optional query clause. html_table(source_object_name, display_field_names, ...[matching_field_name, matching_field_value], additional_clause_optional) -> string

name: LOG
keywords: returns the natural logarithm (base e) of the specified number. log(num) -> decimal

name: IF
keywords: evaluates a logical condition. if true, returns value_if_true. if false, returns value_if_false_optional (if provided); otherwise returns $skip_assignment. if(...[logical_test, value_if_true], value_if_false_optional) -> object

name: INDEX_OF
keywords: returns the zero-based index of the first occurrence of substring within string (case-sensitive). optionally starts searching from index_optional. returns -1 if not found. index_of(string, substring, index_optional) -> integer

name: INDEX_OF_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns the zero-based index of the first occurrence of substring within string(case-insensitive). optionally starts searching from index_optional. returns -1 if not found. index_of_ignore_case(string, substring, index_optional) -> integer

name: IS_ALL_LOWER_CASE
keywords: returns true if the string contains only lowercase alphabetical characters; otherwise, returns false. is_all_lower_case(string) -> boolean

name: IS_ALL_UPPER_CASE
keywords: returns true if the string contains only uppercase alphabetical characters; otherwise, returns false. is_all_upper_case(string) -> boolean

name: IS_ALPHA
keywords: returns true if the string contains only alphabetic characters; otherwise, returns false. is_alpha(string) -> boolean

name: IS_ALPHA_SPACE
keywords: returns true if the string contains only alphabetic characters or spaces; otherwise, returns false. is_alpha_space(string) -> boolean

name: IS_ALPHANUMERIC
keywords: returns true if the string contains only alphabetic characters or numeric digits; otherwise, returns false. is_alphanumeric(string) -> boolean

name: IS_ALPHANUMERIC_SPACE
keywords: returns true if the string contains only alphabetic characters, numeric digits, or spaces; otherwise, returns false. is_alphanumeric_space(string) -> boolean

name: IS_BLANK
keywords: returns true if the value is null, empty, contains only whitespace, or evaluates to $skip_assignment; otherwise, returns false. is_blank(value) -> boolean

name: IS_CURRENT_USER_IN_OWNER_QUEUE
keywords: returns true if the current context user is a member of the record owner's queue. otherwise, returns false. is_current_user_in_owner_queue() -> boolean

name: IS_DECIMAL
keywords: returns true if the string represents a valid decimal number; otherwise, returns false. is_decimal(string) -> boolean

name: IS_EMAIL_ADDRESS
keywords: returns true if the string is formatted as a valid email address; otherwise, returns false. is_email_address(string) -> boolean

name: IS_FIRST_IN_ITERATION
keywords: returns true the first time a given combination of evaluated expression values occurs in the current iteration, and false for any duplicates after. is_first_in_iteration(...expressions) -> boolean

name: IS_INSERT
keywords: returns true if the current action is an insert , otherwise, returns false. in an upsert process where use salesforce upsert api is unchecked, dsp performs matching based on the target matching field and separates records into insert and update actions. use this function to apply different transformations depending on whether a record is being inserted or updated. is_insert() -> boolean

name: IS_NUMERIC
keywords: returns true if the provided string contains only unicode digits; otherwise, returns false. is_numeric(string) -> boolean

name: IS_PHONE_NUMBER
keywords: returns true if the provided string matches a valid phone number format; otherwise, returns false. is_phone_number(string) -> boolean

name: IS_PRODUCTION
keywords: returns true if the current execution is running in a production environment, otherwise, returns false. is_production() -> boolean

name: IS_TARGET_FIELD_ASSIGNED
keywords: returns true if the mapped target field has been processed and assigned a value. returns false if the field was skipped ($skip_assignment) or has not been processed. is_target_field_assigned(mapped_target_field_name) -> boolean

name: IS_UPDATE
keywords: returns true if the current action is an update , otherwise, returns false. in an upsert process where use salesforce upsert api is unchecked, dsp performs matching based on the target matching field and separates records into insert and update actions. use this function to apply different transformations depending on whether a record is being inserted or updated. is_update() -> boolean

name: JOIN_JSON
keywords: returns a filtered array containing objects from the provided json array that match the specified field name and field value criteria. join_json(json_array_string, ...[joining_field_name, joining_field_value])

name: JOIN_OBJECT_CONNECTION
keywords: returns records from a specified object through a named connection or a related connection, filtered by joining field-value pairs, with an optional additional filtering clause. join_object_connection(connection_name, object_name, ...[joining_field_name, joining_field_value], additional_clause_optional)

name: JOIN_OBJECT_SOURCE
keywords: returns records from the specified object via the source connection that match the provided joining field–value pairs, with an optional additional filtering clause. join_object_source(object_name, ...[joining_field_name, joining_field_value], additional_clause_optional)

name: JOIN_OBJECT_TARGET
keywords: returns records from a specified object via the target connection that match the provided joining field–value pairs, with an optional additional filtering clause. join_object_target(object_name, ...[joining_field_name, joining_field_value], additional_clause_optional)

name: JSON_GET_FIELD_VALUES
keywords: returns a list containing the value of the specified field from each map in the provided list. optionally excludes null values from the result. json_get_field_values(json_array, field_name, exclude_nulls) -> list

name: JSON_SERIALIZE
keywords: returns the provided value as a json string. json_serialize(json) -> string

name: JSON_SERIALIZE_PRETTY
keywords: serializes the provided object into a json string with pretty-printed formatting. json_serialize_pretty(json) -> string

name: LAST_INDEX_OF
keywords: returns the starting position (zero-based index) of the last occurrence of substring within string. the search is case-sensitive. if end_position_optional is provided, the search considers characters from the start of the string up to the specified end position. returns -1 if the substring is not found. last_index_of(string, substring, end_position_optional) -> integer

name: LAST_INDEX_OF_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns the starting position (zero-based index) of the last occurrence of substring within string, ignoring case differences. if end_position_optional is provided, the search considers characters from the start of the string up to the specified end position. returns -1 if the substring is not found. last_index_of_ignore_case(string, substring, end_position_optional) -> integer

name: LEFT
keywords: returns a substring containing the specified number of characters from the beginning (left side) of the provided string. if num_chars exceeds the string length, the entire string is returned. left(string, num_chars) -> string

name: LEN
keywords: returns the number of characters in the provided string. len(string) -> integer

name: MATCHES
keywords: returns true if the provided string matches any of the specified regular expressions; otherwise, returns false. matches(string, ...regex_expressions) -> boolean

name: MAP_VALUE_CONTAINS
keywords: returns the corresponding return_value for the first compare_substring found within the provided string (case-sensitive). if no substrings match, returns default_return_value_optional. if default_return_value_optional is omitted and no matches occur, the function returns $skip_assignment. map_value_contains(string, ...[compare_substring, return_value], default_return_value_optional)-> object

name: MAP_VALUE_CONTAINS_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns the corresponding return value for the first compare substring found within the provided string, performing case-insensitive matching. if no substrings match, returns default return value optional. if default return value optional is omitted and no match occurs, the function returns $skip_assignment. map_value_contains_ignore_case(string, ...[compare_substring, return_value], default_return_value_optional) -> string

name: MAP_VALUE_STARTS_WITH
keywords: returns the corresponding return_value for the first compare_substring that matches the beginning of the provided string (case-sensitive). if no substrings match, returns default_return_value_optional. if default_return_value_optional is omitted and no matches occur, the function returns $skip_assignment. map_value_starts_with(string, ...[compare_substring, return_value], default_return_value_optional) -> object

name: MAP_VALUE_STARTS_WITH_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns the corresponding return_value for the first compare_substring that matches the beginning of the provided string, performing case-insensitive matching. if no substrings match, returns default_return_value_optional. if default_return_value_optional is omitted and no matches occur, the function returns $skip_assignment. map_value_starts_with_ignore_case(string, ...[compare_substring, return_value], default_return_value_optional)-> object

name: MAX
keywords: returns the largest number from the given set of numbers. max(...num) -> number

name: MILLISECOND
keywords: extracts the millisecond (0–999) from a datetime value. millisecond(datetime) -> integer

name: MIN
keywords: returns the smallest number from the given set of numbers. min(...num) -> number

name: MINUTE
keywords: extracts the minute (0–59) from a datetime value, based on the context user’s local time zone. minute(datetime) -> integer

name: MINUTE_GMT
keywords: extracts the minute (0–59) from a datetime value, based on gmt. minute_gmt(datetime) -> integer

name: MONTH
keywords: returns the month component (1=january) from a date or datetime, evaluated in the context user's local time zone. month(date/datetime) -> integer

name: NOT
keywords: returns true if the provided logical value evaluates to false; otherwise, returns false. not(logical) -> boolean

name: NOW
keywords: returns the current datetime based on the context user's local time zone. now() -> datetime

name: OR
keywords: returns true if any provided logical condition evaluates to true; otherwise, returns false. or(...logical) -> boolean

name: RANDOMIZE
keywords: returns a randomized value of the same data type as the provided input. supports text, number, date, and boolean values. randomize(text/number/date/boolean) -> same type as input

name: RANDOM_ITEM
keywords: returns a random item from the given set of items. random_item(...item) -> object

name: REPLACE
keywords: returns a new string by replacing all case-sensitive occurrences of a target substring in the original string with a specified replacement. replace(string, target, replacement) -> string

name: REPLACE_ALL
keywords: returns a new string in which all occurrences matching the provided regular expression (regex) within the original string are replaced by the specified replacement substring. replace_all(string, regex, replacement) -> string

name: REPLACE_FIRST
keywords: returns a new string in which only the first occurrence matching the provided regular expression (regex) within the original string is replaced by the specified replacement substring. replace_first(string, regex, replacement) -> string

name: RIGHT
keywords: returns a substring containing the specified number of characters from the end (right side) of the provided string. right(string, num_chars) -> string

name: ROUND
keywords: returns the value rounded to the nearest integer using half-even rounding. round(number) -> integer

name: SCRAMBLE
keywords: shuffle the items in the current batch and select one at random. scramble(value) -> same data type as value

name: SECOND
keywords: extracts the second (0–59) from a datetime value. second(datetime) -> integer

name: SET_SCALE
keywords: rounds a number to the specified number of decimal places using half-even rounding. set_scale(num, num_digits) -> decimal

name: SIN
keywords: returns the trigonometric sine of the specified angle. sin(num) -> decimal

name: SKIP_BLANK_VALUE
keywords: returns the provided value if it is not blank. if the value is blank (null, empty, or whitespace), returns $skip_assignment. skip_blank_value(value) -> object

name: SPLIT
keywords: returns an array of substrings by splitting a string using a regular expression delimiter. split(string, regex) -> string[]

name: STARTS_WITH
keywords: returns true if the provided string starts with any of the specified compare_strings (case-sensitive); otherwise, returns false. starts_with(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: STARTS_WITH_IGNORE_CASE
keywords: returns true if the provided string starts with any of the specified compare_strings(case-insensitive); otherwise, returns false. starts_with_ignore_case(string, ...compare_strings) -> boolean

name: STRING_JOIN
keywords: returns a single concatenated string formed by joining multiple provided objects using the specified separator string. each object is converted to its string representation before concatenation. string_join(...object, separator_string) -> string

name: STRING_APPEND_UNIQUE
keywords: appends an item to an existing string using the specified separator unless the item already exists. string_append_unique(existing_string, item, separator) -> string

name: SUBSTRING
keywords: returns a substring extracted from the provided string, beginning at the start_index (inclusive) and ending at the end_index (exclusive). indexing is zero-based. substring(string, start_index, end_index) -> string

name: SUBSTRING_AFTER
keywords: returns the substring that occurs after the first occurrence of the specified separator within the provided string. if the separator is not found, returns an empty string. the search is case-sensitive. substring_after(string, separator) -> string

name: SUBSTRING_AFTER_LAST
keywords: returns the substring that occurs after the last occurrence of the specified separator within the provided string. if the separator is not found, returns an empty string. the search is case-sensitive. substring_after_last(string, separator) -> string

name: SUBSTRING_BEFORE
keywords: returns the substring that occurs before the first occurrence of the specified separator within the provided string. if the separator is not found, returns an empty string. the search is case-sensitive. substring_before(string, separator) -> string

name: SUBSTRING_BEFORE_LAST
keywords: returns the substring that occurs before the last occurrence of the specified separator within the provided string. if the separator is not found, returns an empty string. the search is case-sensitive. substring_before_last(string, separator) -> string

name: SUBSTRING_BETWEEN
keywords: returns the substring found between the first occurrences of the specified open and close substrings within the provided string. if either the open or close substring isn't found, returns an empty string. the search is case-sensitive. substring_between(string, open, close) -> string

name: TAN
keywords: returns the trigonometric tangent of the specified angle. tan(num) -> decimal

name: TRIGGER_FLIPPER
keywords: this function is used within a before insert or before update trigger to track whether a specific checkbox field (defaulting to false ) has been flipped from false to true . the "flipped" state is recorded in memory only . immediately after tracking the flip, the function resets the checkbox field to false , ensuring that the field remains unchecked in the database. this mechanism allows users to manually trigger actions by checking the field on demand—without persisting the change. if the optional parameter flip_if_evaluated_true_optional is provided and evaluates to true , the function will also treat the field as flipped. this allows you to define automatic rules that simulate a flip and trigger corresponding logic. trigger_flipper(flip_if_evaluated_true_optional) -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_AFTER
keywords: returns true if the current trigger context is an "after" event (after insert, after update, after delete or after undelete); otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_after() -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_BEFORE
keywords: returns true if the current trigger context is a "before" event (before insert, before update, or before delete); otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_before() -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_FLIPPED
keywords: returns true if the specified field's value has changed in the current transaction (i.e., the field was updated or flipped from its previous value). trigger_is_flipped(field_name) -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_CHANGED
keywords: returns true if any of the specified fields have been modified from their previous values during the update dml operation; otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_changed(...field_names) -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_CHANGED_FROM
keywords: returns true if the specified field's value has changed from any of the provided old values in the current trigger context; otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_changed_from(field_name, ...old_values) -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_CHANGED_TO
keywords: returns true if the specified field's value has changed to any of the provided new values in the current trigger context; otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_changed_to(field_name, ...new_values) -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_DELETE
keywords: returns true if the current trigger context involves a delete operation (before delete or after delete); otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_delete() -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_INSERT
keywords: returns true if the current trigger context involves an insert operation (before insert or after insert); otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_insert() -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_UNDELETE
keywords: returns true if the current trigger context is an undelete operation (after undelete); otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_undelete() -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_IS_UPDATE
keywords: returns true if the current trigger context involves an update operation (before update or after update); otherwise, returns false. trigger_is_update() -> boolean

name: TRIGGER_OLD_VALUE
keywords: returns the previous value of the specified field in an update dml operation. trigger_old_value(field_name) -> object

name: TODAY
keywords: returns the current date in the context user's local time zone. today() -> date

name: TO_BLOB
keywords: converts a string (string) into an apex blob type. if the input cannot be converted, the function throws an error. to_blob(string) -> blob

name: TO_BOOLEAN
keywords: converts a string into a boolean value. if the input cannot be converted, the function returns an error. to_boolean(string) -> boolean

name: TO_DATE
keywords: converts a string or datetime value into a date by extracting the calendar date from the input. if the input cannot be parsed, an error is thrown. to_date(string/datetime) -> date

name: TO_DATETIME
keywords: converts a string in a recognized date/time format into a datetime value. the result is returned in gmt. if the input string cannot be parsed, an error is thrown. to_datetime(string) -> datetime

name: TO_DECIMAL
keywords: converts the input value to a decimal. if the input cannot be converted, the function throws an error. to_decimal(string/double/long/float/integer, scale_optional) -> decimal

name: TO_INTEGER
keywords: converts a value to an integer. if the input cannot be converted, the function throws an error. to_integer(string/decimal/double/float/integer) -> integer

name: TO_LOWER_CASE
keywords: converts all letters in the specified text to lowercase. to_lower_case(string, locale_optional) -> string

name: TO_PDF
keywords: creates a binary object out of the given string, encoding it as a pdf file. to_pdf(string) -> blob

name: TO_STRING
keywords: converts the specified value into an unformatted text string. to_string(value) -> string

name: TO_START_OF_MONTH
keywords: returns the first day of the month for a specified date. to_start_of_month(date) -> date

name: TO_START_OF_WEEK
keywords: returns the date representing the first day of the week for a specified date. to_start_of_week(date) -> date

name: TO_TIME
keywords: converts a time string from the context user's local time zone to a time value in gmt. to_time(string) -> time

name: TO_UPPER_CASE
keywords: converts all letters in the specified text to uppercase. to_upper_case(string, locale_optional) -> string

name: TRIM
keywords: returns a string with leading and trailing whitespace removed. trim(string) -> string

name: VALUE_IN
keywords: returns true if the provided value matches any of the specified compare values; otherwise, returns false. value_in(value, ...compare_values) -> boolean

name: VLOOKUP
keywords: performs a dynamic lookup on a salesforce object and returns the specified field value(including relational fields up to 5 levels), from the first matching record. vlookup(target_object_name, return_field_name, ...[matching_field_name, matching_field_value], additional_clause_optional) -> object

name: VLOOKUP_ALL
keywords: queries the specified object and returns the designated fields (plus the record id and lookup field) from all records that match one or more field-value pairs, with an optional additional filtering clause. vlookup_all(target_object_name, return_field_names, ...[matching_field_name, matching_field_value], additional_clause_optional) -> list >

name: VLOOKUP_CONNECTION
keywords: performs a dynamic lookup on a salesforce object through a connection and returns the specified field value (including relational fields up to 5 levels), from the first matching record. vlookup_connection(connection_name, object_name, return_field_name, ...[matching_field_name, matching_field_value], additional_clause_optional) -> object

name: VLOOKUP_RECORD
keywords: performs a dynamic lookup on a salesforce object and returns the full object record from the first record that matches the provided field-value pairs. vlookup_record(target_object_name, ...[matching_field_name, matching_field_value], additional_clause_optional) -> object

name: VLOOKUP_RECORD_CONNECTION
keywords: performs a dynamic lookup on a salesforce object through a connection and returns the full object record from the first record that matches the provided field-value pairs. vlookup_record_connection(connection_name, object_name, ...[matching_field_name, matching_field_value], additional_clause_optional) -> object

name: YEAR
keywords: returns the year component from a date or date time, evaluated in the context user's local time zone. year(date/datetime) -> integer

name: YESTERDAY
keywords: returns the date value representing yesterday, evaluated in the context user's local time zone. yesterday() -> date

name: AGG_AVG
keywords: performs a dynamic aggregation on a specified salesforce object and returns the average of a selected numeric field from all records that match the given criteria. agg_avg(aggregate_object_name, aggregate_field_name, ...[group_field_name, group_field_value], additional_filters_optional) -> decimal

name: AGG_COUNT
keywords: performs a dynamic aggregation on a specified salesforce object and returns the count of records matching the provided conditions. agg_count(aggregate_object_name, aggregate_field_name, ...[group_field_name, group_field_value], additional_filters_optional) -> integer

name: AGG_COUNT_DISTINCT
keywords: performs a dynamic aggregation on a specified salesforce object and returns the count of unique (distinct) values in a selected field for the matching records. agg_count_distinct(aggregate_object_name, aggregate_field_name, ...[group_field_name, group_field_value], additional_filters_optional) -> integer

name: AGG_MAX
keywords: performs a dynamic aggregation on a specified salesforce object and returns the maximum value of a specified field among all matching records. agg_max(aggregate_object_name, aggregate_field_name, ...[group_field_name, group_field_value], additional_filters_optional) -> decimal

name: AGG_MIN
keywords: performs a dynamic aggregation on a specified salesforce object and returns the minimum value of a specified field among all matching records. agg_min(aggregate_object_name, aggregate_field_name, ...[group_field_name, group_field_value], additional_filters_optional) -> decimal

name: AGG_SUM
keywords: performs a dynamic aggregation on a specified salesforce object and returns the sum of the selected numeric field from all records that match the provided criteria. agg_sum(aggregate_object_name, aggregate_field_name, ...[group_field_name, group_field_value], additional_filters_optional) -> decimal

name: $CONTEXT_RECORD_ID
keywords: $context_record_id is used in ui-based rules engines—such as data loader, data list, and action button—to dynamically reference the current record id from the lightning record page. when used in transformations, it is automatically replaced with the record’s id at runtime.

name: $EXECUTABLE_NAME
keywords: $executable_name returns the name of the currently running executable.

name: $EXECUTABLE_ID
keywords: $executable_id returns the id of the currently running executable.

name: $JOINER
keywords: $joiner is a prefix used to reference fields from a dataset that has been joined in the scoping step of an executable (left-join or cross-join). it allows downstream logic—such as scope filter (post join) rules and field mappings—to access the joined record’s fields. for example, $joiner.parent__r.status__c references the status__c field on the joined record’s parent__r relationship.

name: $LAST_EXECUTION
keywords: $last_execution references the most recent execution record for the current executable (any outcome), allowing formulas to read fields from that execution.

name: $LAST_SUCCESSFUL_EXECUTION
keywords: $last_successful_execution references the most recent successful execution record for the current executable, allowing formulas to read fields from that execution.

name: $ORG_DOMAIN_URL
keywords: returns current org's domain url.

name: $SKIP_ASSIGNMENT
keywords: `$skip_assignment` is a special keyword used in dsp formulas to conditionally bypass processing based on dynamic logic. field mapping: if a formula evaluates to `$skip_assignment`, the target field is excluded from the request payload. scope filters: if a formula evaluates to `$skip_assignment`, the source record is omitted from processing. this enables fine-grained control over field-level assignments and record-level processing.

name: $SOURCE_OBJECT_NAME
keywords: returns the resolved input object name for the currently running executable.

name: $TARGET_OBJECT_NAME
keywords: returns the target object name for the currently running executable.

name: $User.FirstName

name: $User.LastName

name: $User.Name
keywords: returns the full name of the running user.

name: $User.ProfileId
keywords: returns the profile id of the running user.

name: $User.Username

name: $User.Id
